To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
testosterone, its metabolites DHT and 3alpha-androstenediol, and their intrahippocampus administration produce analgesia, anxiolysis, and cognitive enhancement.

testosterone (T) administration to gonadectomized rats increases analgesic, anxiety-reducing, and cognitive-enhancement effects, and these effects are mediated in large part by T's nonaromatizable 5alpha-reduction metabolites, dihydrotestosterone and 3alpha-androstenediol, which are elevated in the hippocampus in conjunction with the behavioral effects.

T, DHT and 3alpha-androstane-3alpha,17beta-diol (3alpha-dihydrotestosterone) administration produced analgesia, anxiolytics, and cognitive enhancement concomitant with increased 3alpha-dihyrotestosterone in the hippocampus of male rats.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding how T's effects on anxiety and cognition are mediated.
the role of testosterone and its metabolites in anxiety, analgesia, and cognition.
the role of T metabolites in mediating the effects of T on pain, anxiety, and cognition.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
T, DHT and/or 3alpha-dihydrodiol (3alpha-DIOL) administration to gonadectomized rats produces similar behavioral effects concur with elevating 3alpha-DILO levels in the hippocampal region.

T, DHT and 3alpha-Diol administration produced analgesia, reduced anxiety, and improved cognitive performance concomitant with elevated 3alpha-Dihydrotestosterone in the hippocampus of gonadectomized rats.
T and its metabolites have similar behavioral effects and that these effects may be mediated by 5alpha-reductase metabolites in the brain.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
T, DHT and 3alpha-Diol administration produced similar behavioral effects concommitant with elevating T-metabolites in the hippocampal region.
the behavioral actions of T and DHT may be mediated by actions of 3alpha-dihydrotestosterone in the hippocampus.
testosterone's analgesic/anxiolytic and cognitive-enhancing actions may involve the hippocampal production of the 3alpha-dihydrotestosterone and/or 3alpha-androstane-3alpha, 17beta-diol.
The main takeaway from our work is that
3alpha-dihydrotestosterone and 3alpha-androstenediol, metabolites of testosterone, are likely to mediate some of testosterone's effects on anxiety and cognition in rats.
T metabolites may have a role in the regulation of anxiety-like behavior and cognitive function.
T's effects on pain and anxiety may be mediated by actions of 3alpha-dio in the hippocampus.
